subject: [Incident] Warmup queue overflow in Reserved GPU cluster — next steps and credits
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Patel <jordan@evergreenhealth.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Warmup queue overflow observed in your Reserved GPU cluster — immediate update

Jordan —

Thanks again for the quick call this morning. I wanted to follow up with a concise update: we confirmed an autoscaling warmup regression in your dedicated pool that caused warm instances to not fully attach to the routing mesh between 08:46–09:28 PT today. The symptom you saw (requests queued and elevated latency/500s) maps to that window.

What we did immediately:
- Failed warmup path reverted and warm nodes were forcibly attached (08:59 PT) to restore capacity.
- Temporary scale-up to burst nodes to drain the queue (09:04 PT).
- Routing fallback tightened to prefer healthy nodes by request age (09:12 PT).

Customer impact summary (preliminary):
- Approx 42 minutes of intermittent elevated latency for ~12% of calls to the Reserved cluster.
- A small number of in-flight requests returned errors due to queue timeouts.

Next steps from Redwood:
1) We will share a timeline and root-cause analysis by EOD tomorrow.
2) We propose a goodwill credit to your account to cover excess error/retry costs — draft proposal attached.
3) We want to schedule a technical review with your ops team and our infra leads to walk the timeline and the mitigations we will apply.

I'm looping Dylan and Kim to coordinate the postmortem and to verify the impact numbers. Jordan, could you confirm any downstream consequences (e.g., user-facing errors, billing concerns, or regulatory impact) so we capture everything in the RCA?

Apologies for the disruption — we'll get you a full postmortem with concrete actions to prevent recurrence.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
(attachment: 20280325_warmup_timeline.pdf)
From: Jordan Patel <jordan@evergreenhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-25T09:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Warmup queue overflow observed in your Reserved GPU cluster — immediate update

Marissa —

Thanks for the quick triage. We saw:
- A spike of failed API calls in our integration logs between 08:50–09:20 PT, roughly aligned with your window.
- Two downstream jobs retried automatically; one patient-notification job delayed ~18 minutes (no data loss).
- No HIPAA breach or data export issues, but this did trigger an internal incident at Evergreen Ops which required operator interventions.

We appreciate the proposed credit and want the timeline for our audit log. Please include the exact request IDs for the failures so we can cross-check. Also want to understand whether your burst nodes use the same tenancy/hardware (we rely on pinned nodes for latency guarantees).

Jordan
Ops Lead — Evergreen Health
(attachment: evergreen_impact_summary.csv)
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-25T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Warmup queue overflow — internal triage notes

Team —

Initial notes from infra: the warmup service (node-prep) failed to signal "ready" after image bake due to a race in the KV cache update. The rollout that included a change to the readiness probe went out at 02:10 PT this morning to a subset of Dedicated clusters (canary batch 7). Evergreen's pool was part of that batch.

Impact path: readiness probe regression -> node not marked as ready -> router preserved slot but didn't route -> request age increased -> queue overflow for requests pinned to the pool.

Mitigations in-flight (completed):
- Reverted the readiness change across remaining canary hosts (09:00 PT).
- Forced attach for Evergreen's warm nodes (08:59 PT).
- Added an automated fallback to route around nodes with stale KV timestamps (09:10 PT).

Action items:
- Aditya: assemble request-id list and failure logs for Evergreen (needed by customer).
- Kim: draft EOD RCA and proposed permanent fix plan. Include whether we will revert the readiness probe change entirely or rework it.
- Marissa: coordinate customer comms and the credit note.

Dylan
Director, Infrastructure Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Patel <jordan@evergreenhealth.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-25T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Warmup queue overflow observed in your Reserved GPU cluster — immediate update

Jordan —

Thanks for the quick summary. Attached is a small CSV with the request IDs we saw fail (Aditya pulled these). We validated the failures against our logs; the majority map to the 08:46–09:28 PT window.

Answers to your questions:
- The burst nodes we used are on the same hardware family but are not pinned to your reserved tenancy; they were used only to mitigate the queue backlog. We will not use burst nodes for serving any stateful workloads without explicit coordination.
- We are providing a provisional credit equal to estimated retry/billing impact; draft amount is in attached proposed_credit_amount.txt. This is subject to final reconciliation after we complete the RCA.

Would you be available for a 30-minute technical review at 10:00 PT on Monday (03/27)? We want to walk the timeline, the permanent fix plan, and the monitoring changes we will add (KV timestamp alerting + warmup probe integration tests).

Apologies again for the disruption. We will circulate the full postmortem by EOD Monday and assign an engineer to Evergreen as a single point of contact until the fix is verified in production.

Best,
Marissa
(attachment: proposed_credit_amount.txt)
From: Jordan Patel <jordan@evergreenhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-26T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Warmup queue overflow observed in your Reserved GPU cluster — immediate update

Marissa / Dylan —

Thanks for the follow-ups and for pulling the request IDs. We reviewed the numbers with our compliance and billing teams — the provisional credit looks reasonable. We can take the 10:00 PT slot on Monday for the technical review.

Two asks before the call:
1) Please include a short summary slide in the RCA doc that states the sequence of config change -> rollout -> detection -> mitigation (one slide for our auditors).
2) Confirm the SLO change windows for future warmup-probe flips; we want at least a 24-hour notification for any readiness-related rollout.

We'll join the call with our platform engineer and compliance lead.

Jordan
